learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how post-independence Indian artists experimented with global abstract movements while keeping their roots firmly in Indian soil!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Formed in Bombay in 1947, the PAG (including artists like M.F. Husain, S.H. Raza, and F.N. Souza) wanted to break free from the romantic Bengal School. They embraced global modern art (like Cubism and Expressionism) but painted Indian subjects.
Trained in Paris, she returned to India and painted the sadness and poverty of rural Indians using bold Western oil techniques. She bridged the gap between Europe and India.

Rejecting both Western art and the Bengal School, Jamini Roy found inspiration in the village folk toys and 'Kalighat' patachitra of Bengal. He used thick black outlines and bright, flat earth colors.

Ramkinkar Baij brought modernism to sculpture. His 'Santhal Family' (made of cement and pebbles) was the first public modern sculpture in India, depicting ordinary tribal people instead of kings or gods.

fun_activity.title: 👁️ The Jamini Roy Outline
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a mother and child. Now, trace over your pencil lines with the thickest black marker you have. Color inside the lines using only flat, solid red, yellow, and blue. You just painted in the Kalighat folk style!

exam_tips: 📌 'Mother and Child' is a recurring theme. Know the difference between Jamini Roy's folk style and Amrita Sher-Gil's melancholic oil style.
📌 Ramkinkar Baij is considered the father of modern Indian sculpture. Memorize his masterpiece: 'Santhal Family'.
📌 The PAG (Progressive Artists' Group) was formed in the year of India's independence (1947) to create a new artistic identity for a new nation.
quick_recap: ⭐ Modern Indian art shifted from mythology to the realities of society and the working class.
⭐ Jamini Roy popularized the bold, simple folk art style of Bengal.
⭐ The Progressive Artists' Group integrated Western modernism (like abstract art) with Indian themes.
